claim: TgLMBD3 (TGME49_222200) was assigned as a transmembrane protein of the plasma membrane by hyperLOPIT.
source: During the verification of protein location assignments from our hyperLOPIT spatial proteomic studies, we C-terminally reporter-tagged an uncharacterised protein that we call TgLMBD3 (TGME49_222200) that was assigned as a transmembrane protein of the plasma membrane by hyperLOPIT (Barylyuk et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to hyperLOPIT studies (Barylyuk et al., 2020).

claim: Endogenously reporter-tagged TgLMBD3 shows a distinctive surface location pattern of ~5–8 puncta arranged as a subapical ring at the cell surface.
source: By immunofluorescence assay (IFA) the endogenously reporter-tagged TgLMBD3 showed a distinctive surface location pattern of ~5–8 puncta arranged as a subapical ring at the cell surface (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence assay data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: TgLMBD3 is exclusively located to the Centrin2 apical annuli positions.
source: TgLMBD3 was exclusively located to the Centrin2 apical annuli positions (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Centrin2 is a known marker of the apical annuli.
source: Centrin2 is a known marker of the apical annuli, although it additionally occurs at discrete locations at the conoid, centrosome, and basal complex (Hu et al., 2006; Leung et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Hu et al., 2006; Leung et al., 2019).

claim: TgLMBD3 contains nine transmembrane domains with a cytosolic C-terminal extension.
source: The predicted membrane topology of this new protein includes nine transmembrane domains with a cytosolic C-terminal extension (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane topology prediction shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TgLMBD3 showed rapid trypsin sensitivity in proteolytic shaving assays.
source: TgLMBD3, which migrates as a double band on SDS-polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, showed rapid trypsin sensitivity (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by trypsin shaving assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The surface protein SAG1 was progressively diminished as internal SAG1 pools recycled to the surface.
source: Similarly, the surface protein SAG1 was progressively diminished as internal SAG1 pools recycled to the surface (Gras et al., 2019; Koreny et al., 2023), whereas internal marker proteins (GAP40, PRF, TOM40) were all trypsin-protected by the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Gras et al., 2019; Koreny et al., 2023).

claim: Internal marker proteins (GAP40, PRF, TOM40) were all trypsin-protected by the plasma membrane.
source: Similarly, the surface protein SAG1 was progressively diminished as internal SAG1 pools recycled to the surface (Gras et al., 2019; Koreny et al., 2023), whereas internal marker proteins (GAP40, PRF, TOM40) were all trypsin-protected by the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is supported by trypsin shaving assay data.

claim: The trypsin sensitivity data are consistent with exposure of inter-transmembrane loops of TgLMBD3 at the cell surface.
source: These data are consistent with exposure of inter-transmembrane loops of TgLMBD3 at the cell surface and, therefore, that the apical annuli are structures that extend to the surface environment of the cell.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the trypsin shaving data.

claim: The apical annuli are structures that extend to the surface environment of the cell.
source: These data are consistent with exposure of inter-transmembrane loops of TgLMBD3 at the cell surface and, therefore, that the apical annuli are structures that extend to the surface environment of the cell.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the trypsin shaving data.

claim: TgLMBD3 contains a conserved limb development membrane protein 1 domain (LMBD) that consists of 9 transmembrane helices in a 5+4 arrangement.
source: TgLMBD3 contains a conserved limb development membrane protein 1 domain (LMBD) that consists of 9 transmembrane helices in a 5+4 arrangement (Figure 1B) but whose functions are generally not well studied (Redl and Habeler, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by membrane topology data in Figure 1B and citation to Redl and Habeler, 2022.

claim: Four LMBD orthogroups exist.
source: A global phylogeny of LMBD proteins shows that four LMBD orthogroups exist (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TgLMBD3 belongs to orthogroup III.
source: TgLMBD3 belongs to orthogroup III and, hence, our nominated name for this protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Orthogroup III is widely present in eukaryotes.
source: Although orthogroup III is widely present in eukaryotes, all animals (holozoa) have lost this paralogue, and none have been functionally characterised.
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: All animals (holozoa) have lost the orthogroup III paralogue.
source: Although orthogroup III is widely present in eukaryotes, all animals (holozoa) have lost this paralogue, and none have been functionally characterised.
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Orthologues of TgLMBD3 are retained in all apicomplexans and throughout their close alveolate relatives (including dinoflagellates and ciliates).
source: Nevertheless, orthologues of TgLMBD3 are retained in all apicomplexans, and throughout their close alveolate relatives (including dinoflagellates and ciliates) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The strong conservation of TgLMBD3 throughout Apicomplexa implies that it performs an important function in Toxoplasma.
source: Thus, while a function for TgLMBD3 cannot be readily identified from orthologues, its strong conservation throughout Apicomplexa implies that it performs an important function in Toxoplasma.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from phylogenetic conservation data.

claim: TgLMBD3 is resolved as a small punctum within the Centrin2 rings although slightly peripheral to it by 3D-SIM.
source: Three-dimensional structured illumination microscopy (3D-SIM) resolved TgLMBD3 as a small punctum within the Centrin2 rings although slightly peripheral to it, consistent with TgLMBD3 being in the plasma membrane and Centrin2 associated with the IMC beneath (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D-SIM imaging data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The TgLMBD3-labelled annuli were always positioned at the cisternae boundaries, specifically where the apical cap boundary intersects with the longitudinal suture boundaries.
source: The TgLMBD3-labelled annuli were always positioned at the cisternae boundaries, specifically where the apical cap boundary intersects with the longitudinal suture boundaries (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: All intersections of the apical cap boundary with longitudinal suture boundaries observed contained a TgLMBD3 punctum.
source: All such intersections observed contained a TgLMBD3 punctum and, hence, the variable number of apical annuli from cell to cell is apparently defined by the number of longitudinal IMC boundaries.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data.

claim: The variable number of apical annuli from cell to cell is apparently defined by the number of longitudinal IMC boundaries.
source: All such intersections observed contained a TgLMBD3 punctum and, hence, the variable number of apical annuli from cell to cell is apparently defined by the number of longitudinal IMC boundaries.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from imaging data.

claim: GAP45 and IMC1 both showed an interruption where the TgLMBD3 puncta occur.
source: While both proteins occur throughout the peripheral IMC regions of the cell, both showed an interruption where the TgLMBD3 puncta occur (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: Centrin2 and other markers of the apical annuli are recruited to the IMC during early stages of daughter cell formation.
source: Centrin2, and other markers of the apical annuli, are recruited to the IMC during early stages of daughter cell formation (Engelberg et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Engelberg et al., 2020.

claim: TgLMBD3 only appears at apical puncta as the cell apex emerges from the mother cell at the time of plasma membrane recruitment.
source: Cells captured throughout the process of endodyogeny showed that TgLMBD3 only appears at apical puncta as the cell apex emerges from the mother cell at the time of plasma membrane recruitment (Figure 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Relicts of the mother cell's apical annuli TgLMBD3 persist at the stage when daughter cells emerge.
source: Relicts of the mother cell's apical annuli TgLMBD3 persist at this stage (Figure 3, arrows), suggesting that little or no TgLMBD3 is recycled from mother to daughter.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Little or no TgLMBD3 is recycled from mother to daughter cells.
source: Relicts of the mother cell's apical annuli TgLMBD3 persist at this stage (Figure 3, arrows), suggesting that little or no TgLMBD3 is recycled from mother to daughter.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from imaging data.

claim: The apical annuli provide coordinated gaps in the IMC barrier that forms at the earliest point of IMC development.
source: Collectively, these data imply that the apical annuli provide coordinated gaps in the IMC barrier that forms at the earliest point of IMC development and that they maintain access of the cytosol to these specialised locations in the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from multiple imaging experiments.

claim: The apical annuli maintain access of the cytosol to specialised locations in the plasma membrane.
source: Collectively, these data imply that the apical annuli provide coordinated gaps in the IMC barrier that forms at the earliest point of IMC development and that they maintain access of the cytosol to these specialised locations in the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from multiple imaging experiments.

claim: TgLMBD3 BioID recovered known apical annuli proteins as the most significantly BioID-enriched proteins.
source: This approach recovered known apical annuli proteins as the most significantly BioID-enriched proteins (e.g. AAP2–5, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by BioID proteomics data.

claim: Three SNARE proteins were detected as biotinylated proteins with hyperLOPIT location assignments as integral plasma membrane proteins in TgLMBD3 BioID.
source: Amongst these proteins were three SNARE (soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment protein receptor) proteins, each containing either a Qa SNARE domain (TGME49_209820), Qb SNARE domain (TGME49_306640), or Qc SNARE domain (TGME49_253360).
evidence: The claim is supported by BioID proteomics data and hyperLOPIT assignments.

claim: The three domain-containing SNARE proteins typically function at a target membrane of vesicle fusion by forming heterotetrameric complexes with a vesicle-bound R SNARE which drives the fusion of the vesicle.
source: These three domain-containing proteins typically function at a target membrane of vesicle fusion by forming heterotetrameric complexes with a vesicle-bound R SNARE which drives the fusion of the vesicle (Figure 4A, Jahn and Scheller, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Jahn and Scheller, 2006 and illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: Molecular phylogenies place the Qa SNARE with 'SyntaxinPM' orthologues.
source: Molecular phylogenies place these three proteins with canonical SNARE orthologues: the Qa SNARE with 'SyntaxinPM' orthologues, the Qb SNARE with 'NPSN' orthologues, and the Qc SNARE with 'Syp7' orthologues (Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis and citations to Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017.

claim: Molecular phylogenies place the Qb SNARE with 'NPSN' orthologues.
source: Molecular phylogenies place these three proteins with canonical SNARE orthologues: the Qa SNARE with 'SyntaxinPM' orthologues, the Qb SNARE with 'NPSN' orthologues, and the Qc SNARE with 'Syp7' orthologues (Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis and citations to Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017.

claim: Molecular phylogenies place the Qc SNARE with 'Syp7' orthologues.
source: Molecular phylogenies place these three proteins with canonical SNARE orthologues: the Qa SNARE with 'SyntaxinPM' orthologues, the Qb SNARE with 'NPSN' orthologues, and the Qc SNARE with 'Syp7' orthologues (Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis and citations to Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017.

claim: All three Q SNAREs showed distinct apical annuli locations.
source: All three SNAREs showed distinct apical annuli locations (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TgNPSN is exclusively located at apical annuli.
source: TgNPSN is exclusively located at apical annuli, whereas TgStxPM and TgSyp7 show some additional signal as a single structure in the central region of the cell (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TgStxPM and TgSyp7 show some additional signal as a single structure in the central region of the cell.
source: TgNPSN is exclusively located at apical annuli, whereas TgStxPM and TgSyp7 show some additional signal as a single structure in the central region of the cell (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Super resolution imaging of TgNPSN shows a similar location to TgLMBD3 relative to Centrin2: a small punctum centred on the Centrin2 ring but displaced towards the plasma membrane.
source: Super resolution imaging of TgNPSN shows a similar location to TgLMBD3 relative to Centrin2: a small punctum centred on the Centrin2 ring but displaced towards the plasma membrane (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by super resolution imaging data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The three SNAREs implicate the annuli as sites for exocytic vesicle fusion at the plasma membrane.
source: Together, these SNAREs implicate the annuli as sites for exocytic vesicle fusion at the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the presence of SNAREs at the apical annuli.

claim: All four apical annuli proteins were depleted to undetectable levels within 3–12 hr of auxin (IAA) treatment.
source: All proteins were depleted to undetectable levels within 3–12 hr of auxin (3-indolacetic acid [IAA]) treatment (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The depletion of all four apical annuli proteins showed strong phenotypes of reduced plaque development.
source: Plaque assays assess tachyzoite competence for the entire lytic cycle, and the depletion of all four proteins showed strong phenotypes of reduced plaque development (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by plaque assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Depletion of all four apical annuli proteins resulted in delayed parasite replication at 24 hr post invasion.
source: Depletion of all proteins resulted in delayed parasite replication at 24 hr post invasion (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by replication assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: All mutants showed an average lag of one to three division cycles behind the control.
source: All mutants showed an average lag of one to three division cycles behind the control, with the depletion of TgStxPM showing the most severe retardation of parasite replication.
evidence: The claim is supported by replication assay data.

claim: The depletion of TgStxPM showed the most severe retardation of parasite replication.
source: All mutants showed an average lag of one to three division cycles behind the control, with the depletion of TgStxPM showing the most severe retardation of parasite replication.
evidence: The claim is supported by replication assay data.

claim: The apical annuli are necessary for cell proliferation in the host cell environment.
source: These data show that the apical annuli are necessary for cell proliferation in the host cell environment.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the growth phenotype data.

claim: Depletion of TgNPSN and TgSyp7 showed clear reductions in secreted GRA1 and GRA2 signal.
source: Depletion of TgNPSN and TgSyp7 showed clear reductions in this secreted signal (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: When the secreted GRA1/2 signal was reduced upon apical annuli protein knockdown, the GRA signal seen within the parasite was apparently increased compared to the control.
source: When the secreted GRA1/2 signal was reduced upon apical annuli protein knockdown, the GRA signal seen within the parasite was apparently increased compared to the control (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: No change was evident in either microneme or rhoptry number or staining intensity when any of the four proteins were depleted.
source: No change was evident in either microneme or rhoptry number or staining intensity when any of the four proteins were depleted (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The elevation in dense granule number with apical annuli disruption is specific to this class of exocytic compartments.
source: Hence, this elevation in dense granule number with apical annuli disruption is specific to this class of exocytic compartments.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the observation that micronemes and rhoptries are unchanged while dense granules increase.

claim: For all three apical annuli protein depletions, dense granule proteins overwhelmingly dominated the proteins of increased abundance in the cells.
source: For all three apical annuli protein depletions, dense granule proteins overwhelmingly dominated the proteins of increased abundance in the cells (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative proteomics data shown in Figure 7.

claim: For TgLMBD3 depletion, the GRAs were almost exclusively the proteins whose increase was significant.
source: For TgLMBD3 depletion, the GRAs were almost exclusively the proteins whose increase was significant.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative proteomics data.

claim: The changes in GRA abundances that were assessed as non-significant in all three knockdowns at this timepoint were strongly skewed towards being increased.
source: Even the changes in GRA abundances that were assessed as non-significant in all three knockdowns at this timepoint were strongly skewed towards being increased.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative proteomics data.

claim: Perturbation of apical annuli function results in reduced secretion of dense granule proteins.
source: These data provide further strong evidence that perturbation of apical annuli function results in reduced secretion of dense granule proteins.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the proteomics data showing accumulation of dense granule proteins.

claim: The apical annuli structures span the parasite plasma membrane.
source: The apical annuli structures span the parasite plasma membrane
evidence: This is the title of a results section summarizing findings.

claim: The apical annuli have been previously described as features of the cell's IMC, beneath and separate from the plasma membrane.
source: The Toxoplasma apical annuli have been previously described as features of the cell's IMC, beneath and separate from the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim references prior characterization of apical annuli.

claim: The annuli structures are relevant to the plasma membrane with four integral plasma membrane proteins at these sites including one that is exposed at the cell surface.
source: Here, we show that the annuli structures are relevant to the plasma membrane with four integral plasma membrane proteins at these sites including one that is exposed at the cell surface.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: The annuli occur at small gaps in the IMC where three alveolar vesicles meet (the apical cap vesicle and two lateral vesicles) providing direct access of the cytosol to the plasma membrane.
source: We show that the annuli occur at small gaps in the IMC where three alveolar vesicles meet (the apical cap vesicle and two lateral vesicles) providing direct access of the cytosol to the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: TgLMBD3 is a polytopic protein conserved throughout Apicomplexa and most eukaryotes.
source: One of the apical annuli membrane proteins, TgLMBD3, is a polytopic protein conserved throughout Apicomplexa and most eukaryotes.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from phylogenetic analysis.

claim: The other three apical annuli membrane proteins represent Q SNARE proteins, containing Qa, Qb, and Qc SNARE motifs respectively, which are tethered by C-terminal transmembrane domains.
source: The other three represent Q SNARE proteins, containing Qa, Qb, and Qc SNARE motifs respectively, which are tethered by C-terminal transmembrane domains as is their conventional and ancestral state (SNARE protein fusions, and alternative membrane tethering mechanisms via post-translational added moieties, occur in many systems as derived states) (Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Neveu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim summarizes findings and cites Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Neveu et al., 2020.

claim: Depletion of all four apical annuli membrane proteins affects dense granule secretion.
source: Depletion of all four of these proteins affects dense granule secretion firmly implicating the apical annuli as the site of dense granule docking and membrane fusion.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from knockdown experiments.

claim: The apical annuli are the site of dense granule docking and membrane fusion.
source: Depletion of all four of these proteins affects dense granule secretion firmly implicating the apical annuli as the site of dense granule docking and membrane fusion.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the knockdown experiments.

claim: The functions of LMBD protein family members are not well understood.
source: The functions of this group of proteins, however, are not well understood (Redl and Habeler, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Redl and Habeler, 2022.

claim: The last eukaryotic common ancestor contained multiple LMBD proteins.
source: The four clear LMBD protein orthogroups found throughout eukaryotes suggest that the last eukaryotic common ancestor contained multiple of these proteins.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Dictyostelium has retained genes for all four LMBD orthogroups.
source: While some eukaryotes, e.g., Dictyostelium, have retained genes for all four (Kelsey et al., 2012), most major eukaryotic groups have lost one or more of these paralogues.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Kelsey et al., 2012.

claim: Most major eukaryotic groups have lost one or more LMBD paralogues.
source: While some eukaryotes, e.g., Dictyostelium, have retained genes for all four (Kelsey et al., 2012), most major eukaryotic groups have lost one or more of these paralogues.
evidence: The claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis.

claim: LMBR1 was associated with polydactyly and limb malformations in vertebrates.
source: The first identified protein of this family, LMBR1, was associated with polydactyly and limb malformations in vertebrates, but its molecular role is still unclear (Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022.

claim: LMBR1L interacts with lipocalins and other ligands involved in signalling cascades (Wnt/b-catenin and Nf-kB pathways).
source: Other known members of the family are: LMBR1-like (LMBR1L, also known as LIMR), which interacts with lipocalins and other ligands involved in signalling cascades (Wnt/b-catenin and Nf-kB pathways); LMBR1 domain-containing protein 1 (LMBD1), which interacts with the lysosomal cobalamin transporter ABCD4; and LMBD2, which is a G-protein-coupled receptor-associated regulator of β2-adrenoceptor signalling (Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022.

claim: LMBD1 interacts with the lysosomal cobalamin transporter ABCD4.
source: Other known members of the family are: LMBR1-like (LMBR1L, also known as LIMR), which interacts with lipocalins and other ligands involved in signalling cascades (Wnt/b-catenin and Nf-kB pathways); LMBR1 domain-containing protein 1 (LMBD1), which interacts with the lysosomal cobalamin transporter ABCD4; and LMBD2, which is a G-protein-coupled receptor-associated regulator of β2-adrenoceptor signalling (Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022.

claim: LMBD2 is a G-protein-coupled receptor-associated regulator of β2-adrenoceptor signalling.
source: Other known members of the family are: LMBR1-like (LMBR1L, also known as LIMR), which interacts with lipocalins and other ligands involved in signalling cascades (Wnt/b-catenin and Nf-kB pathways); LMBR1 domain-containing protein 1 (LMBD1), which interacts with the lysosomal cobalamin transporter ABCD4; and LMBD2, which is a G-protein-coupled receptor-associated regulator of β2-adrenoceptor signalling (Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Gyimesi and Hediger, 2022.

claim: TgLMBD3 could contribute to the regulation of dense granule secretion, potentially in response to some extracellular stimulus.
source: While TgLMBD3 is in a different orthogroup to any of these studied paralogues, their common involvement in signalling events suggests that this protein of the apical annuli could contribute to the regulation of dense granule secretion, potentially in response to some extracellular stimulus.
evidence: The claim is speculation based on the functions of related proteins.

claim: SNARE proteins are classically responsible for driving membrane fusion events.
source: SNARE proteins are classically responsible for driving membrane fusion events and our data strongly implicate the roles of TgStxPM, TgNPSN, and TgSyp7 with dense granule fusion with the plasma membrane at the apical annuli.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The data strongly implicate the roles of TgStxPM, TgNPSN, and TgSyp7 with dense granule fusion with the plasma membrane at the apical annuli.
source: SNARE proteins are classically responsible for driving membrane fusion events and our data strongly implicate the roles of TgStxPM, TgNPSN, and TgSyp7 with dense granule fusion with the plasma membrane at the apical annuli.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the study's data.

claim: In other eukaryotes these SNARE orthologues all operate at the plasma membrane.
source: In other eukaryotes these SNARE orthologues all operate at the plasma membrane, and there is no evidence of duplication and/or specialisation of these SNAREs in Apicomplexa (Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017.

claim: There is no evidence of duplication and/or specialisation of these SNAREs in Apicomplexa.
source: In other eukaryotes these SNARE orthologues all operate at the plasma membrane, and there is no evidence of duplication and/or specialisation of these SNAREs in Apicomplexa (Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Dacks and Doolittle, 2002; Klinger et al., 2022; Venkatesh et al., 2017.

claim: Vesicle fusion to a target membrane is driven through the regulated formation of the SNARE complex, a tight four-helix bundle of the Qa, Qb, and Qc SNARE motifs with an R SNARE motif-containing protein.
source: Vesicle fusion to a target membrane is driven through the regulated formation of the SNARE complex, a tight four-helix bundle of the Qa, Qb, and Qc SNARE motifs with an R SNARE motif-containing protein (Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Neveu et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Jahn and Scheller, 2006; Neveu et al., 2020.

claim: The Q SNAREs are anchored to the target membrane.
source: The Q SNAREs are anchored to the target membrane, and this is consistent with our observation of all three SNAREs being stably associated at the apical annuli.
evidence: The claim is based on established SNARE biology.

claim: All three Q SNAREs being stably associated at the apical annuli is consistent with them being anchored to the target membrane.
source: The Q SNAREs are anchored to the target membrane, and this is consistent with our observation of all three SNAREs being stably associated at the apical annuli.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the study's data and SNARE biology.

claim: HyperLOPIT spatial proteomic data assigned all three Q SNAREs as integral proteins of the plasma membrane.
source: Moreover, our hyperLOPIT spatial proteomic data assigned all three as integral proteins of the plasma membrane, so it is unlikely that these SNAREs mediate any direct interaction with the IMC alveolar vesicle membranes despite their proximity (Barylyuk et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to hyperLOPIT data (Barylyuk et al., 2020).

claim: It is unlikely that these SNAREs mediate any direct interaction with the IMC alveolar vesicle membranes despite their proximity.
source: Moreover, our hyperLOPIT spatial proteomic data assigned all three as integral proteins of the plasma membrane, so it is unlikely that these SNAREs mediate any direct interaction with the IMC alveolar vesicle membranes despite their proximity (Barylyuk et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the hyperLOPIT data.

claim: A parallel study by Fu et al., 2023, also identified that these three Toxoplasma SNAREs occur at the apical annuli.
source: A parallel study by Fu et al., 2023, also identified that these three Toxoplasma SNAREs occur at the apical annuli.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Fu et al., 2023.

claim: The differences in knockdown phenotypes of the three SNAREs might be due to differing levels of reduction of dense granule secretion in each SNARE knockdown.
source: These differences might be due to differing levels of reduction of dense granule secretion in each SNARE knockdown, and this could be due to either partial compensation from other cell Q SNAREs, or some residual functional protein in the knockdowns.
evidence: The claim is speculation about the cause of phenotypic differences.

claim: Some SNARE proteins are known to be able to participate in multiple membrane fusion events at different parts of the cell and with different SNARE partners.
source: Some SNARE proteins are known to be able to participate in multiple membrane fusion events at different parts of the cell and with different SNARE partners (Jahn and Scheller, 2006), so a second (or more) role for these SNAREs might also explain their different growth phenotypes upon knockdown.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Jahn and Scheller, 2006.

claim: In none of the SNARE knockdowns were there obvious changes to the biogenesis of rhoptries or micronemes, including differences in their total protein abundances.
source: In none of our SNARE knockdowns did we see obvious changes to the biogenesis of two other post-Golgi compartments, rhoptries, or micronemes, including differences in their total protein abundances, so these SNAREs do not appear to perform essential roles in these processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by the study's data.

claim: These SNAREs do not appear to perform essential roles in rhoptry or microneme biogenesis.
source: In none of our SNARE knockdowns did we see obvious changes to the biogenesis of two other post-Golgi compartments, rhoptries, or micronemes, including differences in their total protein abundances, so these SNAREs do not appear to perform essential roles in these processes.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the study's data.

claim: The growth retardation with apical annuli protein depletion is consistent with the reduced delivery of dense granule proteins into the host where they are required in both the parasitophorous vacuole membrane for harvesting host materials for the parasites' nutrition, and the host cytosol to abrogate host defence mechanisms.
source: Rather, the growth retardation with apical annuli protein depletion, particularly with TgLMBD3 and TgNPSN which are exclusive to these sites, is consistent with the reduced delivery of dense granule proteins into the host where they are required in both the parasitophorous vacuole membrane for harvesting host materials for the parasites' nutrition, and the host cytosol to abrogate host defence mechanisms (Griffith et al., 2022).
